endorsements.quote: In practice, for task-specific diagnostic models, prospective accuracy studies should use adjudicated or probabilistic reference standards and explicitly model of ground-truth uncertainty.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Readiness in Emergency Medicine: Expert Consensus Opinion for Preparing the Workforce

evidence.title: An agentic AI system enhances clinical detection of immunotherapy toxicities: a multi-phase validation study
evidence.outcome: Prospective silent-deployment detection F1 versus retrospective performance
evidence.effect: Retrospective detection macro-F1 0.92; prospective silent deployment over three months (884 notes) detection F1 was 0.72–0.79, revealing lower live-data performance
evidence.quote: In prospective silent deployment over three months (884 notes), detection F1 was 0.72–0.79.
evidence.sample_unit: clinical trial staff participants (316 observations; plus 263 retrospective and 884 prospective notes)

evidence.title: From prediction to practice: machine learning models and real-world interventions for magnetic resonance imaging appointment no-shows in a hospital setting
evidence.outcome: Prospective performance during 13-month silent live test versus retrospective validation
evidence.effect: Silent live test on 5882 appointments revealed AUROC 0.61 and AUPRC 0.24, down from held-out validation AUROC 0.65 and AUPRC 0.29.
evidence.quote: On this dataset, the model achieved an AUROC of 0.61 and an AUPRC of 0.24, a reduction in performance when compared to the validation data performance (AUROC: 0.65, AUPRC: 0.29).

evidence.title: Development and Application of a Machine Learning-Based Screening Model for Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease and Economic Benefit Evaluation: A Real-World Study
evidence.outcome: Prospective accuracy of the RF model on a second-batch cohort, evaluated by AUROC
evidence.effect: Prospective cohort of 74 individuals gave AUROC 0.82, 0.59, and 0.84 for no, mild, and moderate-to-severe NAFLD.
evidence.quote: The 295 cases collected in the first batch were used for model development and software creation, and the developed model was then evaluated in a prospective cohort of 74 individuals in the second batch, achieving AUROC values of 0.82, 0.59, and 0.84 for predicting no, mild, and moderate-to-severe NAFLD, respectively.

evidence.title: From Concept to Clinic: Real World Evidence for Autonomous AI Deployment in Primary Care Telemedicine
evidence.outcome: Prospective diagnostic accuracy
evidence.effect: In a silent-mode evaluation during 2,379 real clinical encounters, the AI's top diagnosis matched the blinded treating clinician in 91.3% of cases.
evidence.quote: The AI’s top-1 diagnosis matched the clinician’s diagnosis in 91.3% of cases overall, increasing to 96.3% among cases meeting a pre-specified safety confidence threshold, and 97.9% in common, lower-complexity conditions that met the same confidence threshold.

evidence.title: A ‘Silent Trial’ Assessing the Accuracy of Large Language Models for Assisting Community Health Workers in Low-Resource Settings
evidence.outcome: Referral accuracy of LLMs run silently on live CHW encounters versus CHW decisions
evidence.effect: Silent trial showed CHW referral accuracy 97.9% (95% CI 96.1-98.9); o3 performed similarly to CHWs, while Gemini 2.5-Flash had 47.3% (95% CI 42.6-52.1), revealing large model differences before activation.
evidence.quote: CHWs demonstrated high referral accuracy (97.9% [95% CI: 96.1%-98.9%]), and OpenAI’s o3 performed similarly to CHWs while Gemini 2.5-Flash showed low accuracy (47.3% [95% CI: 42.6%-52.1%]).

evidence.title: A hybrid machine learning framework to improve prediction of all-cause rehospitalization among elderly patients in Hong Kong
evidence.outcome: Prospective validation of the model's rehospitalisation predictions after a pilot implementation at the hospital
evidence.effect: tZIP prediction of rehospitalisation from 28 to 365 days achieved above 80% discrimination accuracy retrospectively and prospectively in two out-of-sample cohorts, outperforming Cox and linear models.
evidence.quote: The tZIP prediction of rehospitalisation from 28 days to 365 days was achieved at above 80% discrimination accuracy retrospectively and prospectively in two out-of-sample cohorts.

evidence.title: Clinical assistant decision-making model of tuberculosis based on electronic health records
evidence.outcome: Prospective performance of the tuberculosis model in live clinical use after retrospective validation
evidence.effect: Real clinic deployment for 4 months, 692,949 patients monitored, 484 confirmed TB; model predicted 440 cases; positive recognition rate 90.91%, false-negative rate 3.83%.
evidence.quote: The MSI-PTDM prediction model was installed at a doctor workstation and operated in a real clinic environment for 4 months.
evidence.sample_unit: patients monitored in 4-month real clinical deployment

evidence.title: DEPLOYR: a technical framework for deploying custom real-time machine learning models into the electronic medical record
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Prospective silent-trial AUROC versus retrospective AUROC
evidence.effect: Silent deployment revealed prospective AUROC generally several points lower than retrospective, e.g., sodium 0.79 vs 0.71, white blood cell 0.76 vs 0.69, carbon dioxide 0.69 vs 0.62.
evidence.quote: Our silent trial results underscore the necessity of prospective evaluations before ML applications are integrated into clinical work-streams.
evidence.sample_unit: machine learning models (laboratory result classifiers) silently deployed

evidence.title: Sepsis Prediction in Hospitalized Children: Model Development and Validation
evidence.outcome: Prospective performance of sepsis model run in silent mode on live EHR data
evidence.effect: In silent-mode prospective validation in 2019, AUC 0.96 (95% CI 0.95-0.97); Aware tier 100% sensitivity; Alert tier PPV 14% (number needed to alert 7).
evidence.quote: The model was prospectively validated in the electronic health record in silent mode during 2019.

evidence.title: Prospective, multicenter validation of the deep learning-based cardiac arrest risk management system for predicting in-hospital cardiac arrest or unplanned intensive care unit transfer in patients admitted to general wards
evidence.outcome: Prospective performance of predictive model on live production data
evidence.effect: Prospective multicenter evaluation in real-world practice showed DeepCARS AUROC 0.869, superior to MEWS/NEWS, indicating retrospective performance was retained prospectively.
evidence.quote: This prospective study aimed to investigate the predictive accuracy of the DeepCARS™ for IHCA or unplanned intensive care unit transfer (UIT) among general ward patients, compared with that of conventional methods in real-world practice.

evidence.title: Automatic triage of twelve-lead electrocardiograms using deep convolutional neural networks: a first implementation study
evidence.outcome: Prospective performance of ECG triage AI on live clinical data versus final clinical diagnosis triage classes
evidence.effect: Mean concordance statistic 0.96 (95% CI 0.95-0.97); zero ECGs needing policy change or cardiology referral were missed; 2.6% predicted acute did not require follow-up.
evidence.quote: Performance was good with a mean concordance statistic of 0.96 (95% confidence interval 0.95-0.97) when comparing DELTAnet with the clinical triage classes.

evidence.title: Implementation and prospective performance evaluation of an intraoperative duration prediction model using high throughput real-time data
evidence.outcome: Model error vs scheduled duration
evidence.effect: During silent prospective deployment, the ML model had a mean error of 27.19 minutes compared with 51.66 minutes for the bias-corrected scheduled duration.
evidence.quote: Mean continuous ranked probability score for the ML model was 27.19 (standard error 0.016) min compared with 51.66 (standard error 0.029) min for the bias-corrected scheduled duration.

evidence.title: Comparing Clinician Estimates versus a Statistical Tool for Predicting Risk of Death within 45 Days of Admission for Cancer Patients
evidence.outcome: Prospective performance of the model on live admissions before EHR implementation
evidence.effect: Prospective analysis of 1,069 admissions; model AUC 0.834 and extremely well calibrated; subsequently implemented in the EMR.
evidence.quote: This study is a prospective analysis of 1,069 solid tumor medical oncology hospital admissions (n = 911 unique patients) from February 7 to June 7, 2022, at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center.

evidence.title: Preserving Informative Presence: How Missing Data and Imputation Strategies Affect the Performance of an AI-Based Early Warning Score
evidence.outcome: Prospective silent-mode performance of the early warning model on live data
evidence.effect: Model generated real-time predictions undisclosed to clinicians; prospective AUROC 0.918 (full data) on 6039 encounters at an external site.
evidence.quote: The model generated predictions in real-time; however, these predictions were neither disclosed to healthcare providers nor incorporated into clinical decision-making processes.

evidence.title: Prostate Cancer Risk Stratification and Scan Tailoring Using Deep Learning on Abbreviated Prostate MRI
evidence.venue: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
evidence.outcome: Prospective performance of DL model on live bpMRI data
evidence.effect: In the prospective cohort, AUC 0.83 (95% CI: 0.77-0.89) for PI-RADS ≥ 3, with 93% sensitivity and 54% specificity.
evidence.quote: In the prospective cohort, the model achieved an AUC of 0.83 (95% CI: 0.77-0.89) for PI-RADS ≥ 3 classification, with 93% sensitivity and 54% specificity.

evidence.title: Real-world deployment of a fine-tuned pathology foundation model for lung cancer biomarker detection
evidence.outcome: Prospective silent-trial performance of EGFR biomarker on live primary samples (AUC)
evidence.effect: Prospective silent trial on primary samples achieved AUC of 0.890, consistent with retrospective internal 0.847 and external 0.870 performance.
evidence.quote: To evaluate real-world clinical translation, we conducted a prospective silent trial of the biomarker on primary samples, achieving an area under the curve of 0.890.
evidence.country: International (US, Europe, Asia; prospective trial at a single US cancer center)

evidence.title: Prospective validation and real-time implementation of an automated machine learning postoperative mortality prediction model
evidence.outcome: Prospective performance of the implemented model on live EHR data versus retrospective 58-feature model
evidence.effect: Prospective 32-feature model AUROC 0.874 (95% CI 0.860-0.887) versus 0.925 (95% CI 0.900-0.947) for the 58-feature model; AUCPR 0.111.
evidence.quote: The AUROC for the prospectively implemented model was 0.874 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.860-0.887), and the AUCPR was 0.111.

evidence.title: Prospective Diagnostic Accuracy and Technical Feasibility of Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Rib Fracture Detection on Chest Radiographs: Observational Study
evidence.outcome: Prospective performance of passive (silent) AI on live ED chest radiographs versus radiologist reports
evidence.effect: Passive deployment on 23,251 radiographs: sensitivity 74.5%, specificity 93.3%, PPV 24.2%, NPV 99.2%; 14-day GPU outage exposed infrastructure fragility; median inference 10.6 s vs 3.3 h.
evidence.quote: AI operated passively, without influencing clinical decision-making.

evidence.title: Performance of AI vs radiology residents in the detection of intracranial hemorrhage on emergency CT: a real-world analysis
evidence.outcome: Prospective silent-mode AI performance versus radiology residents on live emergency CT
evidence.effect: AI sensitivity 84% and specificity 94.4% vs residents 96.4% and 99.6% (p<0.001); AI did not outperform residents, so silent-mode prospective evaluation exposed underperformance before clinical use.
evidence.quote: Results from the AI software were stored in a separate PACS partition and were unavailable to the radiologists for the case reading.
evidence.country: Not reported (single university hospital; European journal)

evidence.title: Deep learning approach for stroke volume variation estimation: retrospective modeling and prospective deployment in real-world practice
evidence.outcome: Prospective real-time performance of deployed SVVNet against ground truth
evidence.effect: In prospective deployment, the model achieved an MAE of 1.33 and Pearson correlation of 0.87 against ground truth during 67 surgeries.
evidence.quote: In the prospective real-time deployment, our deployed model achieved an MAE of 1.33 and a Pearson correlation of 0.87 against the ground truth.

evidence.title: Automated detection of superior mesenteric artery occlusion on post-contrast CT Using a 3D deep learning model
evidence.outcome: Prospective performance of the model on live CT examinations, including sensitivity, specificity, and QA-confirmed missed findings
evidence.effect: Prospective sensitivity 67.6% and specificity 99.6% (AUC 0.917), versus 50.0% sensitivity on the test set; 237 cases flagged for QA, 83 (35.0%) confirmed as missed SMAO.
evidence.quote: Prospectively, sensitivity was 67.6% and specificity was 99.6% (AUC = 0.917).

evidence.title: Deep learning-based Wilms tumor segmentation to create 3D models for surgical planning: Implementation in the clinical workflow
evidence.outcome: Prospective performance of segmentation model in live clinical workflow versus retrospective validation
evidence.effect: Automated segmentation sufficient in 2/10 patients; 8/10 needed corrections (median 11 min). Median Dice kidney 1.00 (0.58-1.00), tumor 0.98 (0.00-1.00).
evidence.quote: In 2/10 patients the automated segmentation was sufficient to be used directly.

evidence.title: Clinically-applicable prediction of hospital stay and patient similarity retrieval in paediatric cardiology using machine learning
evidence.outcome: Prospective performance of length-of-stay model in silent mode on live NHS admissions
evidence.effect: Random Forest mean precision 0.77 ± 0.03 and sensitivity 0.76 ± 0.04 during silent deployment (1,052 admissions), versus 0.88 ± 0.02 accuracy in retrospective benchmarking.
evidence.quote: The Random Forest model shows mean precision and sensitivity of 0.77  ± 0.03 and 0.76  ± 0.04 during NHS silent deployment (1,052 admissions).

evidence.title: Evaluation of a deep learning model applied to chest X-rays of patients with suspected pneumonia presenting to the emergency department designed to predict admission risk: a retrospective training and prospective non-intervention validation
evidence.outcome: Prospective silent-mode (shadow) performance of admission-risk model on live ED data
evidence.effect: Non-interventional shadow deployment on 3677 patients yielded AUC 0.795; 0.828 for pneumonia-related complaints, 0.755 for non-pneumonia complaints; accuracy 0.751 (PSI threshold), 0.729 (CRB threshold).
evidence.quote: IPRO-X predicted IP admissions with an AUC of 0.795, and in the pneumonia-specific chief complaints, AUC increased to 0.828, whereas in non-related pneumonia chief complaints, the AUC decreased to 0.755.

evidence.title: AI-Guided Surgical Blood Readiness: Overcoming Real-World Challenges in Prospective Validation for Safer, More Efficient Blood Preparation
evidence.outcome: Prospective silent-mode performance versus retrospective test performance, MSBOS, and clinician preordering
evidence.effect: Silent prospective validation (n=24,003) maintained AUROC 0.94 and AUPRC 0.55 (test: 0.94, 0.57); sensitivity 0.72 and PPV 0.34, surpassing MSBOS and clinician behavior.
evidence.quote: Silent prospective validation (n=24,003, transfusion rate 2.18%, 95% CI, 2.07 to 2.46) maintained a 0.94 (95% CI, 0.92 to 0.95) AUROC and a 0.55 (95% CI, 0.51 to 0.60) AUPRC.

evidence.title: Spine patient history-taking: a two phase study of a prompt-engineered large language model assistant
evidence.venue: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
evidence.outcome: Simulation-based evaluation preceding prospective pilot (24 scenarios, 3 surgeons)
evidence.effect: Phase 0 simulation showed mean scores above 4.0/5 across all seven domains before the clinical pilot.
evidence.quote: In simulations, Spine-GPT demonstrated high performance, with mean scores exceeding 4.0 out of 5 across all evaluation domains.

evidence.title: Closing the Loop: A Custom Artificial Intelligence Agent to Improve Detection of Radiologist Follow-Up Recommendations
evidence.venue: NEJM catalyst innovations in care delivery
evidence.outcome: Prospective performance of AI agent on live production data in silent mode before activation
evidence.effect: Model evaluated on 10,000 notes and then during 3 months of silent production mode covering over 120,000 unique imaging studies; balanced accuracy exceeded 97% for identifying follow-up notes.
evidence.quote: Model performance was evaluated on a sample of 10,000 randomly selected radiologist notes and further assessed during 3 months of silent production mode, encompassing over 120,000 unique imaging studies.

evidence.title: Prospective comparison of econometric, machine learning, and foundation models for forecasting emergency department boarding patients
evidence.outcome: Prospective forecast performance on live data during a four-month validation period
evidence.effect: Prospective validation showed VAR+XGBoost and VAR outperformed the baseline at both sites; VAR was then deployed in Mission Control.
evidence.quote: VAR alone performed robustly and outperformed baseline at both sites.
evidence.sample_unit: daily ED boarding volume forecasts at two EDs

evidence.title: Conversational Large Language Models for Vestibular Diagnosis in Outpatient Clinics: Prospective Multicenter Diagnostic Accuracy Study
evidence.outcome: Prospective concordance of agent diagnosis with clinician final diagnosis while clinicians were blinded to agent output
evidence.effect: Agent matched the reference diagnosis in 140 of 176 (79.55%; 95% CI 72.8%-85.2%) patients, with clinicians blinded to agent output.
evidence.quote: The conversational agent matched the reference diagnosis in 140 of 176 (79.55%; 95% CI 72.8%-85.2%) patients.
evidence.sample_unit: outpatients with vertigo or dizziness (prospective clinical evaluation); 227 histories in history-based evaluation

evidence.title: Optimising Pharmacovigilance Efficiency with MLIT (Machine Learning for Intelligent Triage): A Tool for Statistical Safety Alerts
evidence.outcome: Prospective concordance between model predictions and reviewers' decisions on live alerts
evidence.effect: 92% of vaccine alerts closed in alignment with model's top-ranked prediction; 98% within top 3 predictions; comparable results for drug portfolio.
evidence.quote: In the prospective validation phase, 92% of vaccine alerts were closed in alignment with the model's top-ranked prediction, while 98% were closed within the top 3 predictions.

evidence.title: ChatGPT-4o as a decision-support tool in a urological tumour board: a prospective evaluation
evidence.venue: Clinical & translational oncology : official publication of the Federation of Spanish Oncology Societies and of the National Cancer Institute of Mexico
evidence.outcome: Prospective performance of AI with outputs hidden from decision-makers until after consensus
evidence.effect: Outputs revealed only after MTB consensus; recommendation concordance 79.2%, below benchmark; four potentially harmful errors identified without affecting decisions (0/106 attitude change)
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o produced a guideline-informed decision with rationale from de-identified summaries, revealed only after MTB consensus.

evidence.title: Development and prospective evaluation of a machine learning model to predict serious cardiac outcomes among paediatric cardiac inpatients
evidence.outcome: Prospective silent-trial performance versus retrospective validation performance (AUROC, PPV, NPV)
evidence.effect: AUROC 0.88 (95% CI 0.88 to 0.89) retrospective vs 0.82 (95% CI 0.79 to 0.83) in prospective silent trial; PPV 0.19 and NPV 0.97 at retrospective-selected threshold.
evidence.quote: The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.88 (95% CI 0.88 to 0.89) for retrospective and 0.82 (95% CI 0.79 to 0.83) for prospective silent trial phases.

evidence.title: In vivo clinical effectiveness of artificial intelligence screening for acute coronary syndrome: testing real-world performance
evidence.outcome: Agreement of live silent CDS with retrospective model; detection of problems before activation
evidence.effect: Silent pilot showed 96.8% raw agreement, Kappa 91.2% (95% CI 90.7–91.8%); uncovered monitoring data-capture flaw that would otherwise have been missed
evidence.quote: Without this prespecified quality check, we may have missed a major issue and attempted to correct calculation errors that were not actually occurring.

evidence.title: Prospective Shadow-Mode Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence Tool for Intracranial Aneurysm Detection on CT Angiography: Incremental Yield and Operational Impact
evidence.venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
evidence.outcome: Prospective AI vs blinded radiologist performance in shadow mode on live CTAs
evidence.effect: Shadow mode on 3,856 CTAs yielded AI sensitivity 0.846 vs radiologist 0.718, similar specificity (0.987 vs 0.985), and revealed setting-specific variability in operational metrics before activation.
evidence.quote: Sensitivity of AI alone (0.846, 0.787-0.894) exceeded radiologist alone (0.718, 0.649-0.779), with similar specificity (radiologist: 0.985, 0.981-0.989; AI: 0.987, 0.983-0.991).

evidence.title: AI-based delineation based on clinical data in MR-guided brachytherapy for cervical cancer reduces delineation time - A prospective paired trial
evidence.venue: Physica medica : PM : an international journal devoted to the applications of physics to medicine and biology : official journal of the Italian Association of Biomedical Physics (AIFB)
evidence.outcome: Prospective clinical use of AI on live data with oncologist correction
evidence.effect: AI outputs were shown to and corrected by oncologists in live care, not hidden; median mean surface distance between AI and clinical delineations was below 2.1 mm.
evidence.quote: When using AI support, the median of the mean surface distance between the AI and clinically used delineation for all OARs and targets was below 2.1 mm.

evidence.title: Natural Language Processing - A Surveillance Stepping Stone to Identify Child Abuse
evidence.outcome: Whether silent-mode running on live ED notes enabled algorithm refinement before clinical activation
evidence.effect: 73 of 353 notes falsely triggered the NLP, mostly from linguistic-context errors. Common false-positive scenarios were identified and the algorithm was refined to improve specificity.
evidence.quote: Analysis of an NLP algorithm in "silent mode" allowed for refinement of the algorithm and highlighted areas in which real-time CDS may help ED providers identify and pursue appropriate evaluation of injuries associated with child physical abuse.

evidence.title: In vitro to in vivo translation of artificial intelligence for clinical use: screening for acute coronary syndrome to identify ST-elevation myocardial infarction
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Agreement of silent in vivo CDS with in vitro model; errors detected
evidence.effect: Over a 2-month silent pilot of 18,335 encounters, raw agreement 95.5% (CI 95.2%-95.9%), kappa 87.6% (CI 86.7%-88.6%); additional coding errors identified and corrected.
evidence.quote: CDS fidelity to the model reflected raw agreement of 95.5% (CI, 95.2%-95.9%) and kappa of 87.6% (CI, 86.7%-88.6%).

evidence.title: Sisyphus' Alert: The Uphill Struggle to Improve Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis Clinical Decision Support
evidence.outcome: Alert firing frequency during silent testing before release
evidence.effect: Silent testing showed the initial alert fired an average of 11,154 times per week, prompting significant logic refinements before release.
evidence.quote: The initial alert fired an average of 11,154 times per week when tested silently, prompting significant refinements before release.

evidence.title: Large-scale AI-guided liver malignancy diagnosis: multicenter study and a single-arm trial
evidence.outcome: Prospective performance of AI for liver malignancy diagnosis in live clinical workflow, primary endpoint AUC
evidence.effect: Single-arm trial in 10,333 patients met primary endpoint (lower CI bound >0.900), AUC 0.952 (95% CI: 0.942-0.961).
evidence.quote: The trial met its primary endpoint, defined as an AUC for malignancy diagnosis with the lower bound of the 95% CI exceeding 0.900, achieving an AUC of 0.952 (95% CI: 0.942-0.961).

evidence.title: UWF-FM: A Foundation Model for Comprehensive Ultra-Widefield Retinal Assessment
evidence.outcome: Processing success, inference time and workflow disruption during silent deployment on consecutive examinations
evidence.effect: 100% processing success rate, median inference time ~1.1 seconds per examination, no workflow disruption across 37,665 consecutive examinations.
evidence.quote: During retrospective and prospective silent deployment involving 37,665 consecutive examinations, UWF-FM achieved a 100% processing success rate, a median inference time of approximately 1.1 seconds per examination, and no workflow disruption.
evidence.sample_unit: UWF images read in randomized crossover multi-reader study (four ophthalmologists)

evidence.title: Development and prospective evaluation of a machine learning model to predict vomiting among pediatric cancer and hematopoietic cell transplant patients
evidence.outcome: Prospective silent-trial AUROC versus retrospective AUROC for vomiting prediction
evidence.effect: AUROC 0.730 (95% CI 0.694-0.765) retrospective vs 0.716 (95% CI 0.649-0.784) in the prospective silent trial; performance was retained, with no notable degradation.
evidence.quote: This model retained satisfactory performance in a prospective silent trial.
evidence.sample_unit: admissions (7,408 retrospective plus 340 prospective silent trial)

evidence.title: Prospective pilot evaluation of a deep learning model for kidney stone detection on CT using a web-based workflow platform
evidence.outcome: Prospective forward-in-time performance of the model outside routine clinical operations
evidence.effect: Over six months, three radiologists annotated 5,152 slices; the model achieved 97.83% accuracy, 94.64% sensitivity, 98.27% specificity, 88.50% precision, and kappa 0.90.
evidence.quote: The pilot deployment demonstrated strong diagnostic performance under real-world variability, achieving 97.83% accuracy, 94.64% sensitivity, 98.27% specificity, 88.50% precision, and a Cohen's kappa of 0.90.

evidence.title: Diagnostic accuracy, fairness and clinical implementation of AI for breast cancer screening: results of multicenter retrospective and prospective technical feasibility studies
evidence.outcome: Whether noninterventional prospective deployment revealed problems missed by retrospective validation
evidence.effect: Prospective deployment at 12 sites (9,266 cases) confirmed technical feasibility but revealed a distribution shift requiring threshold recalibration.
evidence.quote: Prospective deployment confirmed technical feasibility but revealed a distribution shift requiring threshold recalibration.

evidence.title: Large Language Model Recommendations for Empiric Antibiotics Versus Clinician Prescribing: A Non-Interventional Paired Retrospective Antimicrobial Stewardship Analysis
evidence.outcome: Feasibility of retrospective shadow-mode evaluation of LLM antibiotic recommendations on real admissions
evidence.effect: LLM recommendations generated post hoc, hidden from clinicians, with no influence on care, were evaluated on 493 admissions; guardrail violations 4.9% for LLM vs 17.0% for clinicians.
evidence.quote: We therefore evaluated whether post hoc LLM-generated empiric antibiotic recommendations showed greater concordance with a pre-specified stewardship benchmarking framework than clinician-initiated regimens in a retrospective shadow-mode setting.

evidence.title: Clinical decision support in hematological malignancies using a case-grounded AI agent
evidence.outcome: tumor board concordance in a prospective silent trial
evidence.effect: achieved 82.8% concordance on 64 consecutive, unselected cases run in a silent trial
evidence.quote: External validation on 555 independent cases from a second academic center yielded 81.8% concordance across 47 entities, and a prospective 1-month silent trial on 64 consecutive, unselected cases achieved 82.8% concordance.

evidence.title: An agentic AI system enhances clinical detection of immunotherapy toxicities: a multi-phase validation study
evidence.outcome: Prospective silent-deployment detection performance compared with retrospective performance
evidence.effect: Retrospective detection macro-averaged F1 was 0.92 (263 notes); prospective silent-deployment detection F1 was 0.72–0.79 over three months (884 notes).
evidence.quote: In prospective silent deployment over three months (884 notes), detection F1 was 0.72–0.79.

evidence.title: From prediction to practice: machine learning models and real-world interventions for magnetic resonance imaging appointment no-shows in a hospital setting
evidence.outcome: Prospective predictive performance compared with retrospective validation
evidence.effect: Across 5882 appointments over 13 months, prospective AUROC was 0.61 and AUPRC 0.24, compared with validation AUROC 0.65 and AUPRC 0.29.
evidence.quote: On this dataset, the model achieved an AUROC of 0.61 and an AUPRC of 0.24, a reduction in performance when compared to the validation data performance (AUROC: 0.65, AUPRC: 0.29).

evidence.title: Prospective Real-Time Validation of a Lung Ultrasound Deep Learning Model in the ICU
evidence.outcome: Prospective real-time bedside accuracy versus blinded expert annotation
evidence.effect: Real-time inference accuracy 95%, sensitivity 93%, specificity 96% for B line pattern; previously validated model performed equally well in real time at bedside.
evidence.quote: When compared with gold standard expert annotation, the real-time inference yielded an accuracy of 95%, sensitivity of 93%, and specificity of 96% for identification of the B line pattern.

evidence.title: DEPLOYR: a technical framework for deploying custom real-time machine learning models into the electronic medical record

evidence.outcome: Retrospective versus prospective AUROC during silent deployment
evidence.effect: Retrospective versus prospective AUROC: white blood cell, 0.76 [0.74, 0.79] versus 0.69 [0.68, 0.70]; sodium, 0.79 [0.75, 0.82] versus 0.71 [0.70, 0.72].

evidence.effect: Sensitivity 0.921 (95% CI 0.792-0.973), specificity 0.802 (0.735-0.856), AUC 0.885, accuracy 0.824; high sensitivity but moderate specificity in live bedside use.

evidence.title: Building and Prospectively Evaluating a Prediction Model to Forecast Urgent Dialysis Needs across Four Tertiary Hospitals

evidence.effect: Retrospective MAE was 3.0 (hospital A) and 1.5 (hospital B); in prospective silent deployment ARIMA MAE was 2.2 and 1.5, so no degradation was seen.

evidence.title: Development and Validation of an Automated, Real-Time Predictive Model for Postpartum Hemorrhage

evidence.effect: Derivation AUC 0.81; temporal validation AUC 0.80; prospective real-time automated data (928 patients) AUC 0.82 (95% CI 0.73-0.91), so no performance degradation.
evidence.quote: The model maintained performance in prospective, automated data collected with the predictive model in real time (AUC 0.82 [95% CI, 0.73-0.91]).

evidence.title: Prospective validation of clinical deterioration predictive models prior to intensive care unit transfer among patients admitted to acute care cardiology wards

evidence.effect: Among 5184 display-off visits (311 ICU transfers), AUCs ranged 0.725 to 0.737; models well-calibrated despite five years' passage and COVID-19.

evidence.title: Development, deployment, and continuous monitoring of a machine learning model to predict respiratory failure in critically ill patients
evidence.outcome: Prospective versus retrospective predictive performance during silent deployment
evidence.effect: During 1-month silent deployment, AUC was 0.908 versus cross-validation median 0.897 (IQR: 0.892-0.904); prospective sensitivity was 0.632, specificity 0.849, and PPV 0.235.

evidence.title: Development and Implementation of Automated Referral Triaging System for Spinal Cord Stimulation Procedure in Pain Medicine

evidence.effect: Cross-validation TPR 77.3%, TNR 73.0%; implementation TPR 64.7%, TNR 87.2%, so FPR fell 12.8% and TPR fell 12.6%.
evidence.quote: The one-year implementation results showed TPR of 64.7% and TNR of 87.2%, which reduced FPR by 12.8% while reduced TPR by 12.6%.

evidence.title: A Rule-Based Automated Triage Model Using Natural Language Processing for Pain Medicine-Development and Implementation

evidence.quote: The implementation accuracy of 200 cases for the first 3 months was consistent with our prediction at 83.5%, which concluded that the improvement over ML models (p-value = 0.018) was statistically significant at 95% significance level.

evidence.title: An Open-architecture AI Model for CPT Coding in Breast Surgery: Development, Validation, and Prospective Testing
evidence.outcome: Prospective performance of CPT code extraction model on new operative notes after retrospective validation
evidence.effect: Prospective testing on 268 notes (May-October 2024) confirmed strong real-world performance, consistent with cross-validation AUPRC of 0.976 (compact) and 0.981 (large).
evidence.quote: Prospective testing on 268 notes confirmed strong real-world performance.

evidence.title: Deep learning models for acute kidney injury prediction: multi-center external validation and evaluation under simulated continuous monitoring conditions
evidence.outcome: Prospective-style performance and alert burden under simulated continuous monitoring versus single-point evaluation
evidence.effect: Highest single-point AUROC model (Masked CNN, 0.961) had worst deployment profile (NNE 17.6-564), while ITE-Transformer (AUROC 0.924) had NNE 1.5-2.4; longer horizons showed unstable trajectories.
evidence.quote: Notably, the highest single-point AUROC model (Masked CNN, 0.961) had the worst deployment profile (NNE 17.6-564), while ITE-Transformer (AUROC 0.924) achieved the most favourable alert burden (NNE 1.5-2.4).

evidence.title: Clinical decision support in hematological malignancies using a case-grounded AI agent
evidence.outcome: Prospective silent-trial concordance with tumor board decisions
evidence.effect: 1-month silent trial on 64 consecutive cases: 82.8% concordance (53/64), comparable to retrospective/external performance.
evidence.quote: HemaGuide achieved 82.8% concordance (53/64), with entity-group rates of 81.6% for lymphomas (31/38), 82.4% for PC dyscrasias (14/17) and 88.9% for leukemias (8/9) ( κ = 0.795) (Fig. 6c,d ).

commentary.bottom_line: Silent-mode evaluations on live data sometimes found drops from retrospective results, such as a white blood cell classifier falling from AUROC 0.76 to 0.69, and in other studies performance held steady. No study compared patient outcomes after activation between tools that did and did not go through a silent phase, so certainty that the practice prevents harm is low.

perspectives.view: Most tests are single-site prospective cohorts with no comparison of a silent phase against no silent phase. The two studies labeled randomized appear not to have randomized the silent phase itself. Several studies show that silent runs can reveal gaps, with one reporting F1 of 0.72 to 0.79 against 0.92 retrospectively. Indirectness to patient outcomes lowers certainty.

Silent evaluation found failures before patients were exposed. An emergency CT tool reached 84% sensitivity against 96.4% for residents. One language model reached 47.3% referral accuracy against 97.9% for health workers. A 14-day GPU outage occurred during passive deployment. These results suggest the phase may catch errors, though no study tracked harm after activation.

Silent runs showed workflow and data problems that retrospective testing may not reveal. A segmentation tool needed corrections in 8 of 10 patients, taking a median of 11 minutes. A sepsis alert tier had a PPV of 14%. A model reduced from 58 to 32 features for live EHR use had an AUROC of 0.874, compared with 0.925 retrospectively.

One test ran silently on 429 community health worker encounters in Rwanda that the study described as rural, low-income, and limited English or non-English. Another included older adults in Hong Kong. No test enrolled United States Medicaid or safety-net patients, so live performance gaps for those groups remain unmeasured.

Silent phases in these studies lasted from about one month to thirteen months. One health system ran 20,334 laboratory classifiers silently, which suggests the approach can operate at scale. No study reported the staffing, computing, or delay costs of the silent period, so administrators cannot yet weigh its cost against what it finds.

commentary.research_gap: No study compares tools activated after a silent phase with tools activated without one on post-activation errors, patient harm, or deactivation rates. No study defines how long a silent phase should last or what performance drop should block activation. No study reports the resource cost of silent deployment.
commentary.underserved_note: One silent trial included limited English proficiency, low-income, and rural populations, but it took place among community health workers in Rwanda. No test included United States Medicaid, safety-net, or low-literacy populations, so it is unknown whether silent-mode findings reflect performance for those patients in this country.
